title: Phaedo Consultation Policy
description: Subject-authored standing guardrails that OVERRIDE the inferred consultation signal (Phaedo Protocol v0.1 §10.5). DEPRECATED as a standalone array as of Proposal 0007: authored authorizations are now `standing_rules` entries with `kind:"authorization"` (the single authored home, fingerprint.schema.json). This schema is retained for (a) the back-compat read path — existing `phaedo_consult_policies` / `phaedo_fingerprint.consult_policies` documents stay valid and are still honored by the resolver — and (b) the `$defs.match` / `$defs.effect` subschemas shared by both `consult_policies.rules[]` and `standing_rules` (authorization variant). Removed in v0.2 with the §5 User Configuration migration.

match.description: All present constraints must hold for the rule to apply. Shared by consult_policies.rules[] and standing_rules (kind:authorization).

domains.description: Substring match (case-insensitive) on the action descriptor's domain.

amount_gt.description: Numeric FLOOR: matches only when the action descriptor carries an `amount` strictly greater than this (e.g. escalate irreversible spend over 5000). No amount on the action → the threshold rule does not fire.

amount_lt.description: Numeric CEILING: matches only when the action descriptor carries an `amount` strictly less than this (e.g. auto-proceed reversible purchases under 75). Like `amount_gt`, an action with NO amount does NOT satisfy it — on a relaxing rule an unpriced action must not slip under a ceiling that cannot be checked. Combine with `amount_gt` for a band; both must hold.

effect.description: Force effects (escalate/require_human→escalate, decline, autoproceed→proceed) are authored authorizations: they set the signal at confidence:1.0, deference:high. bias_* nudges one step along proceed→proceed_with_note→clarify→escalate (keeps the inferred confidence).

note.description: Surfaced to the agent as the rationale_hint.

expires_at.description: OPTIONAL RFC 3339. Conditional/revocable authority (§10.5): once this instant passes the authorization is LAPSED and no longer applies (a time-bound, identity-free form of revocation). ENFORCED by the reference resolver — the direction is always authority-narrowing, so it is fail-safe.

require_binding.description: OPTIONAL (§10.5). When true, this rule applies only to a request carrying a valid §10.2 `action_binding`. ENFORCED for authority-EXPANDING effects only (`autoproceed`, `bias_bold`) — a rule that makes the agent more deferential keeps applying regardless, or the gate would become a way to shed a guardrail by omitting a field. Authority-narrowing, like `expires_at`. Subjects SHOULD set it on any new `autoproceed`; a producer that PROPOSES an authorization MUST set it.

agents.description: OPTIONAL, ENFORCED — scope this authorization to specific PAIRED CLIENTS. Entries are opaque, phone-issued client_id values (compared exactly, case-sensitive), matched against the RESOLVER'S OWN identity from its pairing record — never against the self-asserted agent_id, which remains an untrusted audit label. NARROWING-ONLY: an agents-scoped rule is inert for an unlisted or unpaired resolver only when its effect would EXPAND autonomy (autoproceed / bias_bold); a restrictive effect keeps applying regardless, or scoping would become a way to shed a guardrail by running an unlisted client. Inert means 'does not apply' — never broader, never an error. ABSENT and EMPTY differ and the difference is load-bearing: omitting the field leaves the rule unscoped (applies to every client), whereas an empty array is a scope that names no client and therefore matches none. An authoring surface that deselects every client MUST write [] and MUST NOT omit the field, or it would silently grant universal autonomy. Entries MUST be strings; non-string entries are dropped rather than coerced.

revoked.description: OPTIONAL — TOMBSTONES for rules the subject has REVOKED (§10.5). Multi-device sync reconciles guardrail sets by UNION (losing an explicit decision is never acceptable), and a union cannot express a deletion: removing a rule from `rules` on one device is undone by the other device's copy on the next sync, so the revocation silently fails. A tombstone records the removal itself. A consumer MUST drop any rule whose identity appears here, and a merge MUST union tombstones from BOTH sides — a revocation the other device has not yet seen must still take effect. Deliberately FAIL-CLOSED: a tombstoned identity stays revoked even if a rule bearing it reappears (e.g. from a restored backup), because a revoked `autoproceed` returning to life is the harmful direction and rule ids are unique-by-construction. Tombstones may be capped by COUNT but MUST NOT be pruned by age — a device that synced before the prune would resurrect the rule. Distinct from `expires_at`, which lapses an authorization on a schedule the subject set in advance; this records a decision taken after the fact.

id.description: The revoked rule's identity — its `id`, or for a legacy id-less rule the same content-derived key the merge uses to dedupe it. Must be computed identically by every implementation or the tombstone will not match the rule it is meant to kill.

at.description: OPTIONAL RFC 3339 instant of the revocation. Advisory: used to order tombstones when capping by count, never to expire one.
